analysis: The PR is CI, docs and test-only. It touches no provider runtime, coordinator wire contract, attestation, key custody or prefix-cache code, so T-041 and TB-002/003/007/009/011 are unchanged. The main security change is a new 'Choose this job's Actions cache' step. It sets CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off for darkbloom-* runners with no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL. Every actions/cache restore and save step is gated on it. The gated steps are in provider-ci-build/action.yml, provider-release-build/action.yml, ci-master.yml, provider-tests.yml and landing.yml. That stops Darkbloom Sandbox guests reaching GitHub's shared cache. In ci-master.yml and provider-tests.yml a pre-checkout validator discards a cached .git that is a symlink or non-directory, holds symlinks or non-sample hooks, or whose config sets core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or an include, then runs fsck. This is hardening over base, but it is a denylist (one low finding). Saves remain limited to master/dev pushes, and PRs never save. Actions stay SHA-pinned, permissions are read-only, and persist-credentials is false. Release and signing workflows reportedly keep literal Blacksmith labels (A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054). Routing changes move GPU shards and desktop-package to routed Darkbloom lanes. Only test and docs assertions were seen, not the workflow YAML for darkbloom-route.yml, desktop.yml, provider-plan.yml or the later provider-tests.yml hunks. Open questions: whether routed jobs keep read-only permissions and no signing credentials, whether fork PRs stay excluded, and whether every cache step in all workflows honors the gate. Several analyses flagged these as unverified, hence deeper review is advised.

findings.detail: The new 'Discard a damaged or unsafe cached .git' step (also replayed in ci-master.yml) rejects a restored .git only if it has a symlink, a non-sample hook, or a config setting core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or include/includeIf. The comment claims the restored .git 'runs nothing', but the check is incomplete. Keys such as filter.<name>.smudge/clean/process (paired with an uninspected .git/info/attributes), core.sshCommand, core.pager, core.askpass, credential.helper, diff.external, gpg.program, alias.* and uploadpack.packObjectsHook can still execute commands or redirect git when the following checkout and git steps read that config. A poisoned cache entry, for example one saved from a compromised push to master or dev, could then run code on the runner. This is residual hardening incompleteness, not a regression versus base, which only ran fsck. Fix: allowlist expected config keys, or rewrite .git/config to a minimal set, reject .git/info/attributes, or restore only objects and packs.
findings.title: Restored-.git sanitizer is a denylist; other config keys can still run code during checkout
